title: Stop hook auto-closes tasks; agent finish overrides
context: Of 107 tasks in 7 days, only 7 became records: agents often left tasks open, shell edits missed pre-edit hooks, and follow-up prompts ("status", "next") spawned empty rows. Gap between ledger and usable graph records. Touches invariant(s): con_03a0b94b2e (The agent hook must never block an edit on failure: any error exits 0 and never denies; after the event is recognized it emits at most one 'grounding unavailable' context line, unrecognized input emits nothing); con_91e6074b66 (Capability pages for functionality shipped in the current release must state that it ships today and must not retain the stale banner 'In development for the next release.').
decision: Stop hook closes the prompt's task as a host close when the turn ends—provisional, reopened by the next observation, final when agent calls finish/interruption. Tasks with observations become records without agent calling finish. Verification hangs release after timeout + 1min grace.
consequences: Empty follow-up prompts enrich their parent task record instead of leaving ledger-only rows.
Agent-side finish remains authoritative and overrides host close.
Tasks with observations are persisted to graph even if agent never calls finish.
Hung verifications no longer freeze task lifecycle indefinitely.
Implicit task grouping (episode continuations) reduces noise in ledger.
alternatives_rejected: Keep agent-driven closing only: resulted in many unclosed tasks never reaching graph.
Close all unfinished tasks at End: loses provisional semantics and agent override capability.
Create separate records per follow-up prompt: fills ledger with empty rows, obscures intent.
